title: John 16 is no warrant for Mass, saints, or images — heretics used the same text
source_text: V. Multo minus vero possunt nobis fidem facere, multa illa, quae Christus discipulis dicenda habebat, esse traditiones illas, quas nobis hodie obtrudunt de Missae sacrificio, de invocatione Sanctorum, de cultu imaginum, aliisque hujusmodi: certe istud majori cum ratione non affirmant de suis traditionibus, quam prisci haeretici de figmentis & somniis suis, quibus audacia simili authoritatem atque fidem conciliare conabantur: Testatur enim August. tractatu in Joan. 97. veteres haereticos his verbis Christi abusos fuisse, ut figmenta sua populo commendarent, quasi essent illa ipsa quae Christus dicenda discipulis habebat. Omnes, inquit, insipientissimi haeretici qui se Christianos vocari volunt, audacias figmentorum suorum hac occasione Evangelicae sententiae colorare conantur, ubi Dominus ait, adhuc habeo multa vobis dicere. Unde patet Pontificios imitari palam veteres haereticos, dum ex iisdem Christi verbis pro traditionibus suis non scriptis argumentantur.
pass_a_gloss: Much less truly can they make us believe that those many things which Christ had to say to the disciples are those traditions which they thrust upon us today concerning the sacrifice of the Mass, concerning the invocation of the Saints, concerning the worship of images, and other things of this kind: certainly they do not affirm that of their traditions with greater reason than the ancient heretics did of their figments and dreams, by which with similar boldness they tried to win authority and faith: For Augustine in the tract on John 97. testifies that the ancient heretics abused these words of Christ, so that they might commend their figments to the people, as if they were those very things which Christ had to say to the disciples. All the most foolish heretics, he says, who wish to be called Christians, try by this occasion of the Evangelical sentence to color the audacities of their figments, where the Lord says, I still have many things to say to you. Whence it is plain that the Pontificians openly imitate the ancient heretics, while from the same words of Christ they argue for their unwritten traditions.
pass_b_english: Rome may not map John 16 onto Mass sacrifice, saint-invocation, or image-worship.
Ancient heretics used the same verse to baptize their figments.
Augustine (tract on John) already called out that abuse.
So the Pontifician move repeats the old heretical color, not a new proof.

choices.english: that the Pontificians openly imitate the ancient heretics
